description: The generated NAME of an unaliased select item, all live-verified. A (possibly parenthesised, possibly qualified) column reference is named after the COLUMN - (amount), ( amount ), ((amount)) and s.amount all project AMOUNT. EVERY other expression is named by its SOURCE TEXT, bluntly: whitespace and newlines survive exactly as written, nothing is truncated, a parenthesised expression keeps its parens in the name, and a FROM-less literal is named after itself, so SELECT 1 projects a column named 1. A set operation takes its names from the FIRST branch. A positional item is named in its dollar form, $N, and not after the COLUMN<N> name it resolves through; an out-of-range one is refused in that same form. Converted from query/DerivedColumnNameTest. The class's CASE claims - that the text folds to upper case, that a quoted column reference keeps the column's own case, and that a quoted alias is verbatim while an unquoted one folds - are NOT expressible here: the suite schema's column comparison is case-INSENSITIVE, so those assertions would pass vacuously. They stay in the trimmed Java class, which keeps the two tests whose whole subject is case. Everything else - the text, the spacing, the parens, the quoting inside the text, the absence of truncation, and the values - is asserted here.
